Role Description Who we are: At UST, we help the world’s best organizations grow and succeed through transformation. Bringing together the right talent, tools, and ideas, we work with our client to co-create lasting change. Together, with over 30,000 employees in 30+ countries, we build for boundless impact, touching billions of lives in the process. Summary: UST is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Java Full Stack Developer with 5+ years of experience in designing, developing, deploying, and supporting enterprise-scale applications. The ideal candidate will possess strong expertise in Java technologies, Spring Boot, Microservices, React, AWS cloud services, and modern DevOps practices. This role requires a hands-on professional who can contribute across the full software development lifecycle while ensuring application scalability, reliability, security, and performance. The Opportunity: As a Java Full Stack Developer, you will be responsible for building modern full-stack applications, developing cloud-native microservices, and driving engineering excellence through best practices, automation, and continuous improvement. Key Roles & Responsibilities: Design, develop, and maintain scalable backend services using Java, Spring Framework, and Spring Boot. Build responsive, intuitive, and high-performing user interfaces using React. Design and implement Microservices-based architectures for enterprise applications. Develop, maintain, and optimize RESTful APIs and backend integrations. Deploy and support cloud-native applications on AWS services including EC2, ECS, Lambda, S3, and RDS. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver highly scalable and resilient solutions. Implement containerization and deployment strategies using Docker and CI/CD pipelines. Monitor application performance and troubleshoot production issues. Ensure application security, reliability, scalability, and adherence to coding standards. Participate in architecture discussions, technical design reviews, code reviews, and Agile ceremonies. Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives by adopting modern development and DevOps practices. Mentor junior developers and support technical knowledge sharing across teams. What You Need: Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in Java Full Stack Development. Strong expertise in Java 8/11/17, Spring Framework, and Spring Boot. Experience designing and implementing Microservices Architecture. Hands-on experience developing RESTful APIs using Java technologies. Strong frontend development experience with React.js, JavaScript, and TypeScript. Experience deploying and managing applications on AWS cloud platforms. Hands-on experience with Docker and CI/CD implementation. Strong understanding of software design principles, scalability, and performance optimization. Experience working in Agile/Scrum environments. Excellent analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills. Strong communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills. Required Skills: Java 8/11/17 Spring Framework Spring Boot Microservices Architecture REST APIs React.js JavaScript/TypeScript HTML5 & CSS3 AWS (EC2, ECS, Lambda, S3, RDS) Docker CI/CD Pipelines Git Desired Skills: Apache Kafka Kubernetes Redis Terraform Event-Driven Architecture Experience with cloud-native application development. Knowledge of distributed systems and scalable architecture patterns. AWS Certification(s) preferred. Experience in performance tuning and application optimization. Experience leading technical discussions and mentoring team members. Qualification: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline. What We Believe : We’re proud to embrace the same values that have shaped UST since the beginning. Since day one, we’ve been building enduring relationships and a culture of integrity. Today, those same values inspire us to encourage innovation from everyone, champion diversity and inclusion, and place people at the center of everything we do. Humility: We will listen, learn, be empathetic, and help selflessly in our interactions with everyone. Humanity: Through business, we will better the lives of those less fortunate than ourselves. Integrity: We honour our commitments and act with responsibility in all our relationships. Equal Employment Opportunity Statement UST is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Comply with all Company policies and procedures. About Potpie Potpie is building the foundation layer for spec-driven development in large, complex codebases. We focus on making software systems understandable, debuggable, and operable through structured context and AI agents. This is not about incremental tooling. This is about rethinking how software systems are built, evolved, and scaled. Role We are looking for a Full Stack Developer who can think in systems and build end-to-end products with clarity and ownership. This is not a task-driven role. You will be expected to take ideas, shape them into products, and iterate quickly based on real usage. What You Will Do Build and ship end-to-end features across frontend and backend Design scalable APIs and services that power AI-driven workflows Work closely with research and product teams to translate ideas into usable systems Own performance, reliability, and developer experience of the product Experiment rapidly and iterate based on feedback Contribute to architectural decisions as the system evolves Write clean, maintainable, and well-documented code What we are looking for Strong fundamentals in computer science and system design Experience building full stack applications (frontend + backend) Ability to move fast from idea to production Comfort working in ambiguity and taking ownership Good communication skills and ability to collaborate across teams Tech stack (indicative, not restrictive) Frontend: React / Next.js Backend: Node.js / Python / Java / C / C++ Databases: PostgreSQL, Redis Infrastructure: AWS / GCP Experience with APIs, microservices, and distributed systems Bonus Experience building developer tools or platforms Familiarity with AI/ML systems or LLM integrations Understanding of codebases at scale (monorepos, large systems) Contributions to open source projects Why should you join Potpie? You will be working at the intersection of AI and real-world software systems. The goal is not just to build features, but to shape how modern software is developed and maintained. Strong customer pull We are already seeing real demand from enterprise customers. This is not speculative. Teams are actively looking for a solution like this, and we are in the middle of that demand curve already working with F500s and public companies. Deployed with leading enterprises The product is already live in real-world environments with enterprise customers. You won’t be building in isolation, you’ll be shaping a system that is actively used in production. At an inflection point We have early validation, a growing pipeline, and clear momentum. More importantly, we are solving a very critical problem in software engineering that every large team struggles with today. The need for this is widely acknowledged, and the opportunity ahead is significant. The next phase is about scaling execution and capturing that opportunity. Venture-backed with momentum We’ve recently raised capital and have the backing to move fast. The focus now is execution, growth, and building a category-defining company. Define a foundational layer for engineering If we get this right, Potpie becomes a foundational layer for how modern engineering systems are built and operated inside enterprises globally. Meaningful upside as an early leader You will be one of the early hires shaping the company. This comes with competitive compensation and significant ESOP ownership. Given the stage we are at today, the upside on ESOPs over the next 3 to 4 years can be substantial with good execute. Direct message the job poster from Aurora Energy Research Deepa Yadav Deepa Yadav Talent Acquisition Manager- APAC & Early Careers at Aurora Energy Research ( Ex-BlackRock, Fractal Analytics) About the position Based in Gurugram, you will lead our newly established software team (currently four engineers) as we enter an exciting new phase of expansion. We are seeking an Engineering Manager who will build a strong, happy, high-performing team, creating the environment, clarity, and support that enables people to do their best work. This is a people-first role: you will have proven strength in leadership, scaling teams, and developing others. You will report to the Head of Software Product Engineering. Aurora’s mission is to help drive the energy transition through data-driven energy market intelligence and software that supports decision-makers across the power system. You will partner closely with colleagues in Oxford and across the business to help the team build customer-facing software that delivers on this mission. Our platform includes microservices and modern web applications (TypeScript/Node, React, AWS). While this is a leadership-focused role, you will still do some hands-on senior engineering work, contributing code when needed, leading by example on quality, and helping the team make sound technical decisions. You will establish the people and process foundations for an effective engineering team: regular 1:1s, coaching and feedback, inclusive ways of working, and strong delivery practices (planning, stand-ups, reviews, and retrospectives). A key part of the role is growing the team through hiring, attracting, assessing, and onboarding great talent in Gurugram. Key responsibilities Lead and grow the Gurugram engineering team, creating a positive, inclusive, high-trust culture with strong team health and engagement. Hire, onboard, and retain great engineers, owning the hiring process end-to-end in partnership with HR and engineering leadership. Coach, mentor, and develop team members through 1:1s, goal setting, feedback, and growth plans; support performance management when needed. Contribute as a senior engineer: write and review code, guide architecture and technical design, and continuously raise the bar on engineering standards (testing, reliability, and maintainability). Run effective engineering processes and ceremonies (planning, daily coordination, reviews, and especially high-quality retrospectives) that drive continuous improvement and predictable delivery. Partner with Product and stakeholders to shape priorities, manage expectations, and ensure the team delivers valuable outcomes with a sustainable pace and high quality. What we are looking for Required attributes: Strong people leadership and emotional intelligence: able to build trust, communicate clearly, handle difficult conversations, and foster psychological safety. Proven experience coaching, mentoring, and developing engineers (including regular 1:1s, feedback, goal setting, and progression support), with a genuine interest in people development. Demonstrated hiring capability: defining roles, running structured interviews, assessing both technical and behavioural skills, and making high-quality hiring decisions. Experience running effective team processes (e.g., planning, reviews, and retrospectives) and using outcomes to drive continuous improvement. Able to lead within a distributed environment and collaborate effectively with Oxford-based colleagues through proactive communication and inclusion. Experience working hands-on with our (or similar) stack: Node/TypeScript, ExpressJS, React, SQL/NoSQL, AWS and microservices. Strong organisational skills: can balance competing priorities, create clarity, and follow through on commitments. Desirable attributes: Experience using delivery metrics (e.g., DORA) to inform team practices. Experience with engineering quality practices such as unit testing and CI/CD pipelines. What we Offer A fun, informal, collaborative and international work culture A competitive salary package Access to regular coaching and mentoring sessions and the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals Access to the Aurora Academy, our training programme offering a range of opportunities to develop your skills within the responsibilities of your role and within the wider context of the industry. About FurtherAI We're building the AI agents that run insurance — a trillion-dollar industry still powered by manual work. We've raised $30M+ from a16z, YC, Nexus, South Park Commons, and Converge, grown 10x in the last 12 months, and work with top 10 insurance carriers and brokers, plus Fortune 100 companies. Both founders are engineers, and engineers have an outsized say on product direction. The role Nobody owns our frontend today. It's grown to ~690K lines of TypeScript/React across ~2,250 files — a workflow builder, a citation-backed document viewer, data grids holding tens of thousands of rows, a chat assistant, and live views of agents running for minutes at a time. Features ship every week, but the parts nobody owns pile up: two generations of the workflow builder running side by side mid-migration, the same component built three times, performance with good tooling and no one driving it. We're not hiring you to clean up after us. We're hiring you to decide what "good" looks like here, say it out loud, and make it true — while the product keeps shipping. What you'll own Architecture and stack. State, data fetching, routing, module boundaries, build tooling — what we keep, what we drop, what we add. Today: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, Radix, TanStack Query, Bun. You decide what it looks like in a year. One component system. We have ~90 shared primitives and 231 Storybook stories, and we still write the same component twice. Pick the one that wins, migrate the product onto it, and put a gate in place so it stays that way. Performance as a number, not a vibe. Our home route ships ~567KB of gzipped JS before a user can interact. We have bundle budgets, Lighthouse in CI, real-user vitals, and a Sentry digest — nobody's driving them. Own the number, move it, and tell us by how much. Product craft. Work with our designers as a peer — critique their work, fill the gaps, hold opinions on layout, density, motion, and hierarchy, and argue for them. A codebase that's safe for coding agents to touch. A large share of our code now arrives from coding agents. Typed boundaries, lint rules, visual regression tests, and fast feedback loops are what make that safe at our speed — you design for it. The engineers around you. Review, mentor, and hold the bar on every frontend change, across India and the US. Two concrete examples of the kind of problem this role exists to solve: converging our two live generations of the workflow builder into one without freezing the product for a quarter, and designing the interaction patterns for agents that stream partial results over minutes — there's no established playbook for this yet, you'd be inventing ours. What we're looking for 8+ years building production frontend, deep in React and TypeScript — you've shipped customer-facing product fast and lived with the consequences afterward. You've owned a frontend codebase, not just features inside one: architecture, build tooling, component systems, test strategy, release safety. Demonstrated performance practice — you've held a number and moved it. We'll ask which one and by how much. Real product taste — you can look at a screen and say precisely what's wrong with it and why. Sharp with coding agents — you push back on what they write rather than merge it on faith, and you build the checks that make agent-written code safe to ship. A clear writer — we make most decisions in writing, across time zones. Bonus: design systems experience, data-dense or document-heavy products, 0-to-1/early-stage work, B2B SaaS, LLM-backed interfaces. Location and hours Remote in India, Bangalore preferred (where most of engineering sits), but open countrywide. Our designers and part of engineering are in San Francisco; you'll overlap with them roughly 9 PM–2 AM IST. Outside of that window, working hours are flexible to manage.
